probe_plan: Backbone traps are TR1 (route of direct versus indirect against the inferior epigastric vessels), TR31 (cause, congenital versus acquired), TR23 (clinical picture), TR8 with TR9 (strangulation risk and the groin versus inguinal scope word) and TR16 with TR17 and TR7 (which operation for whom). Meet them in this order. First TR1, TR2, TR28 and TR40 together as the anatomy block, since TR40 supplies a distractor for TR1, TR21 and TR9. Then TR31, TR23, TR21 and TR22, which re-use the TR1 position rule in clinical form. Then TR8, TR9 and TR5, which share the 'qualifier changes the superlative' skill and compete in the same stems. Then TR11 and TR12 as the diagnosis and emergency block. Then TR7, TR16, TR17 and TR39 as the operation block, because their options reuse each other (herniotomy, Lichtenstein, Bassini, laparoscopic). Finally TR14 and TR25 (laparoscopic hazards) and TR34 (eponym matching) in the exam-trap and consolidation segments. Every trap has a first probe that surfaces it and a later probe in a different form; TR2, TR25 and TR31 have three. Shared options: TR40 serves as a distractor in TR1, TR21 and TR9 probes, and TR22 in a TR40 probe, but each option maps to exactly one trap. Merged traps: TR3 into TR2, TR6 into TR5, TR13 into TR12, TR26 into TR25, TR32 into TR31. The 43-trap brief was capped at 20.
